Appreciate the context. Legal review notes and recommended compromise below (see attached redline-comments-Karthik-20260303.pdf):

1) Auto-renew: we should keep the standard 12-month auto-renew but offer a 60-day opt-out window prior to renewal date. Rationale: preserves forecast while giving the customer a predictable opt-out mechanism.

2) Notice window for non-renewal/cancellation: I agree 45 days is short. Recommend we counter at 60 days. If customer insists on 45, we can accept for this account only if they agree to a 60-day transition assistance obligation in the TfC clause.

3) Termination for Convenience (TfC): Legal is generally reluctant to grant an unrestricted TfC because of capacity and revenue forecasting impacts. Possible compromise language: BluePeak may terminate for convenience with 60 days' written notice, Redwood will provide reasonable transition assistance (KV cache handoff/docs + data export), and customer will pay a termination fee equal to one month of the average monthly committed spend (calculated on the last three invoices) unless the Order Form total ARR is < $50k, in which case no fee. Alternatively, we can limit TfC applicability to pilots or trial orders only.

4) Operational protections: add a short carve that allows Redwood to deny TfC within the first 90 days of any initial committed term for operational onboarding costs.

Next steps: If commercial is happy with the fee/exception approach, ask Contract Ops to draft an amendment that: (a) adds 60-day opt-out at renewal; (b) updates notice to 60 days; (c) inserts the limited TfC language above with the termination-fee calculation; and (d) includes a one-time transition assistance SLA for up to 60 days post-termination. I attached tracked-comment suggestions for redlines.

Karthik
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference

Vivek — thanks for the quick internal review. A few points from our side:

- On notice, BluePeak prefers 45 days but will consider 60 if Redwood can cap the termination fee or provide an alternative like pro-rated credits (we prefer no flat fee).
